posts.title: Agentic AI Automates RTL Waveform Analysis And Debugging (Columbia, Google)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Columbia University, Google DeepMind, and Google published a technical paper titled “Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification.” Abstract “The unprecedented computational scale of modern artificial intelligence depends on complex, multi-billion-transistor Systems-on-Chip, yet the workflows that verify these chips remain stubbornly manual. Although Large Language Models... » read more
The post Agentic AI Automates RTL Waveform Analysis And Debugging (Columbia, Google) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from Columbia and Google introduced 'Back-to-the-Future' (BTTF), an agentic framework designed to automate post-simulation verification and waveform debugging in chip design.
The framework addresses a critical industry bottleneck where 74.6% of current AI-EDA research focuses on static RTL generation rather than the labor-intensive verification phase.
BTTF utilizes a multi-agent orchestration engine that converts natural-language queries into SQL to analyze massive simulation dumps, achieving 95.33% execution accuracy across a 150-query benchmark.

By normalizing unstructured simulation data into SQLite databases, the system enables automated correlation between signal anomalies and versioned RTL code, significantly reducing manual debugging efforts.

posts.title: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
posts.summary: MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of science and technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can read more from the series here. Late last month, Anthropic released a report arguing that the model GLM-5.3 poses a major cyberattack risk. The report’s core concern is that the…
bullets: The debate over open-source AI models is driven by a conflict between safety advocates, who fear misuse by bad actors, and proponents who argue for democratization and reduced corporate control.

Commercial incentives are heavily influencing the discourse, with hardware providers like Nvidia supporting open models to drive hardware sales, while frontier labs like Anthropic advocate for tighter control.
The industry is currently navigating a complex trade-off between the practical benefits of accessible AI and the systemic risks posed by powerful, modifiable models.

posts.title: BYD launches Da Han EV from $35,050 with up to 1,008 km range
posts.summary:
The Da Han EV comes standard with a 102.3-kWh second-generation Blade Battery that charges from 10% to 97% in just 9 minutes.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD launched the Da Han EV flagship sedan with prices ranging from 235,900 to 275,900 yuan, significantly lower than initial pre-sale levels.
The vehicle features a 102.3-kWh second-generation Blade Battery capable of charging from 10% to 97% in just 9 minutes.
The lineup offers high-end performance, with the top-tier all-wheel-drive variant achieving a 0-to-100 km/h acceleration time of 3.3 seconds.
Standard equipment includes the God's Eye B LiDAR-based driver-assistance system and DiSus-A dual-chamber air suspension.

posts.title: China NEV market share in September: BYD leads with 22.8%, Tesla rises to fourth
posts.summary:
Tesla's share rose to 6.0%, while Li Auto and Nio dropped out of the top 10 in NEV retail sales.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD continues to dominate the Chinese NEV retail market with a 22.8% share, selling 246,816 vehicles in September.
Tesla China's retail sales rebounded 29.6% month-on-month to 64,837 units, elevating its market share to 6.0%.
Geely maintained the second spot with an 11.0% market share, while Leapmotor held third place despite a 7.9% month-on-month decline in sales.
The overall market saw Li Auto and Nio drop out of the top 10 retail rankings for the month.
